comparison: Both evaluations find the core finding SUPPORTED that food intake enhances hippocampal SWRs with dose-dependent effects. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and experimental design details (38 session pairs, appropriate controls), while peer reviewers focus on overall convincingness. OpenEval includes C24 and C92-C93 which peer review addresses separately.

Perfect agreement on SUPPORTED status for mediation analysis claims (C25-C27, C94-C95, C97). Both recognize the importance of disentangling sleep quality from direct food effects. OpenEval provides more technical detail about the statistical approach, while peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge as part of well-performed experiments.

Complete agreement on SUPPORTED status for ad libitum feeding experiments (C28-C31, C75, C96, C98). Both recognize this demonstrates SWR enhancement is not merely recovery from hunger-induced impairment. OpenEval discusses asymmetric hypothalamic responses; peer reviewers accept as part of overall satiety modulation demonstration.

Both find SUPPORTED for the critical caloric vs. sensory control experiment. OpenEval covers C32-C35, C63-C65, C87-C88 while peer review addresses C32-C35, C87-C88. OpenEval emphasizes this as a key mechanistic finding; peer reviewers note it demonstrates caloric content dependence without questioning the design.

Divergent evaluations of hormone experiments (C36-C39, C81, C89-C91, C99). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to acknowledged experimental limitations that may have obscured satiety hormone effects, making mechanistic picture incomplete. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, finding the ghrelin effects and negative results for other hormones compelling and aligned with hormone functions.

Both find SUPPORTED for fiber photometry evidence of hippocampal-hypothalamic communication (C6, C40, C84-C85). OpenEval notes strong statistical significance but emphasizes this is correlational, not causal evidence. Peer reviewers accept the finding without challenge as part of the overall experimental demonstration.

Divergent evaluations of speculative mechanistic claims (C66-C68, C70). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting these are untested predictions requiring additional causal experiments. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, accepting these as reasonable interpretations and promising future research directions. OpenEval also includes C69 which peer review addresses separately.

Both find SUPPORTED for the control finding that NREM duration does not change with food intake (C24). OpenEval includes this with the main food intake findings (R1), emphasizing it strengthens specificity to SWR properties. Peer reviewers address it separately as an accepted control analysis.

Both address the conclusion that satiety state modulates SWRs (C69). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN as part of broader speculative claims requiring causal validation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing this as a convincing conclusion from the data. This represents a key difference in how directly the data support this interpretive claim.

OpenEval evaluates background/context claims (C1-C2, C7-C16) about established knowledge and prior findings as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers typically focus on novel findings rather than literature review accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C17-C18, C41-C43, C52, C72-C74, C76-C80, C82, C86) about metabolic regulation and hormone functions as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are contextual knowledge claims rather than novel experimental findings.

OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C44-C51) about hippocampal roles in feeding regulation as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers do not separately assess background literature accuracy.

OpenEval evaluates background claims (C53-C58, C71) about SWR properties and functions as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these provide context rather than novel findings requiring peer assessment.

OpenEval evaluates anatomical connectivity claims (C59, C83) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as these are established anatomical facts providing framework for interpretation.

OpenEval evaluates methodological details about experimental materials (C60-C65) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as peer reviewers do not separately assess factual material specifications, though these claims overlap with R4's caloric control experiment.
